content.6.3 Devices under evaluation: Cardiac contractility modulation (CCM) evaluated in patients with NYHA class III–IV HF, with LVEF ~25% to ~45% and QRS duration <130 ms; associated with small improvement in exercise tolerance and quality of life. Technologies modifying autonomic nervous system activity (e.g., baroreflex activation therapy) show modest improvements in effort capacity and QOL, but current evidence is insufficient to support specific guideline recommendations for mortality or hospitalization reduction; see gaps in Evidence (section 16).
content.7 Heart failure with mildly reduced ejec: Section header introducing HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF).
content.7.1 The diagnosis of heart failure with: Diagnosis of HFmrEF requires symptoms/signs of HF and a mildly reduced EF (41–49%). Elevated natriuretic peptides support diagnosis: BNP ≥35 pg/mL or NT-proBNP ≥125 pg/mL. Other supportive evidence includes structural heart disease (e.g., increased left atrial size, LVH, echocardiographic measures of LV filling), though these are not mandatory if LVEF measurement is certain. Algorithm referenced in Figure 1 and investigations in Table 5.
content.7.2 Clinical characteristics of patients: Clinical characteristics overlap across LVEF categories. Patients with HFmrEF tend to be more similar to HFrEF than HFpEF: more commonly men, younger, and more likely to have coronary artery disease (approximate CAD prevalence cited as 50–60%); less likely to have atrial fibrillation and non-cardiac comorbidities. Ambulatory HFmrEF patients have lower mortality than HFrEF and are more similar to HFpEF. HFmrEF may include patients whose LVEF improved from ≤40% or declined from ≥50%.
content.7.3 Treatments for patients with heart f: As with other HF forms, diuretics should be used to control congestion. No substantial prospective randomized controlled trials performed exclusively in HFmrEF; some subgroup data from HFpEF trials exist but none met primary endpoints. Strong recommendations about specific therapies cannot currently be made; a Table of Recommendations is included to guide management.
